scope: Curated review of all canonical brain/research checklist tasks, their explicit experimental ideas, the completed frozen measurements, and historical model-search records. Related tasks may map to the same claim; engineering work is kept distinct from falsifiable research.
policy: Execution status describes work; outcome describes evidence for the question. A closed engineering task never counts as a supported research hypothesis.

Supported/refuted applies only to the stated frozen scope. Untested means no qualifying test; inconclusive means available observations do not settle the stated question. Deferred records a work decision, not a negative finding.

Historical conditional labels, current structural observations and controlled/independent validation are separate evidence sources. No modern real-spend accuracy, address recovery or common ownership has been validated by these studies.
Reviewed date is this ledger review, not a fabricated task-creation, closure or experiment date. Study timestamps are taken only from saved artifacts.
Questions summarize the existing notes and recorded studies; their wording does not imply a preregistered hypothesis or experimental protocol.

entries.question: Can bounded scoring and isolated ML work keep collection advancing as the dataset grows?

task_refs.title: Batched scoring and incremental cloud analysis.
Resource metrics and ML failure isolation.

entries.theoretical_conclusion: Memory/time budgets and fixed-snapshot equivalence checks are needed before accepting batch or incremental execution changes.
entries.measured_conclusion: The proposed per-phase resource study, equivalent batched scorer, incremental graph update and separately isolated ML worker are not completed. Existing live services do not validate these optimization claims.
remaining: Measure scanning, analysis, training, scoring and export costs independently.
Compare fixed-model candidate scores and failures under bounded work, preserving publication when ML fails.

entries.question: Can first resolutions, retractions and hypothesis upgrades be distinguished from new imported singletons?
entries.theoretical_conclusion: Net snapshot totals do not identify when an old ambiguous ring was solved. Event-level denominators are needed for a solve-rate claim.
entries.measured_conclusion: Current charts and counts distinguish singleton and multi-member populations, but this dedicated event-transition ledger and eligible cohort solve rate remain open.
remaining: Record first deterministic and retraction/upgrade events with original membership scope and eligible multi-member counts.

entries.question: Can changes in dataset identity, conflicts, negative deltas and publication lag produce explainable alerts?
entries.theoretical_conclusion: An alert needs the triggering snapshots and a distinction between new data, revised analysis and missing coverage.
entries.measured_conclusion: Snapshot progress is displayed, but no completed regression-alert system retains and classifies all proposed triggers.
remaining: Implement snapshot-backed trigger records and explicit resolution reasons without calling net growth a solve count.

entries.question: Can every numerical conclusion be checked against a frozen artifact while study, implementation and deployment states remain distinct?
entries.theoretical_conclusion: Checklist closure and a successful deployment cannot validate a scientific hypothesis. Claim values, denominators and provenance need separate checks.
entries.measured_conclusion: The three historical cards now have an explicit 85-claim manifest and eight rate/denominator checks. A controlled accepted-study-to-deployed-model example remains open; the latest FA2 study did not change the deployed scorer.
remaining: Record one controlled accepted study, selected implementation and deployed version independently.

entries.question: Do repeated scoring and verification preserve earlier runs and replayable candidate scores?
entries.theoretical_conclusion: Immutable runs permit later evaluation and audit, while a reproducible inference artifact alone does not establish forward generalization.
entries.measured_conclusion: Prediction/scaler artifacts, source and feature context, append-only verification events and atomic rollback are implemented and tested. A real-model smoke check replayed saved scores; no new quality gain follows from that infrastructure.
remaining: Complete P2 label eligibility and temporal evaluation before claiming forward accuracy.

entries.question: Do the preserved autoresearch logs establish a comparable model improvement or modern accuracy?
entries.theoretical_conclusion: Historic logged numbers require common datasets, split/label procedures and frozen artifacts before they can be compared or generalized.
entries.measured_conclusion: The archived Markdown records a GBM baseline at 86.1% holdout; the TSV separately records 100.0% values for early configurations and 86.3% for a working-tree feature change. Their common eligible denominator, temporal/graph independence and complete run provenance are unavailable; these are historical reports, not a current benchmark.
remaining: Retain the logs without combining their figures.
Run the explicit P2/P4 protocol for a new comparable result.

entries.question: Are candidate groups stable across added blocks and small score-threshold changes, and does stability predict controlled-label correctness?

task_refs.title: G3 — Cluster validation (P3; depends on G2).

entries.theoretical_conclusion: Persistence may reflect popular decoys or a systematic modeling error; stable membership alone does not establish ownership.
entries.measured_conclusion: No validated cluster population, threshold/seed comparison or stability-versus-correctness evaluation has been completed.
remaining: After controlled group validation, measure merge/split and weak-bridge behavior across predeclared runs.
Test stability against controlled labels and matched null graphs before using it as a confidence signal.

entries.question: How consistently do independently selected sources agree on sampled block hashes, transactions and origins?
entries.theoretical_conclusion: RPC structural checks and a provider’s synchronized/untrusted fields are not independent consensus validation. Different endpoints may share infrastructure.
entries.measured_conclusion: The saved audits used one external RPC. No declared multi-source agreement study with independently assessed source provenance has been completed.
remaining: Record source identity limitations and compare exact hashes and sampled origin/transaction data with an independently selected source.
Retain missing, conflicting and unavailable observations instead of assuming agreement.

evidence.scope: Fixed stratified sample of nonzero-amount output references from heights 0–58,900; one external RPC; v1 did not fingerprint WAL state.

entries.question: How representative are later-verified predictions of all saved and unscorable rings?

task_refs.title: P3 — Calibration and abstention (P1; depends on P1–P2).

entries.theoretical_conclusion: Verification depends on which rings later acquire eligible deterministic evidence. Accuracy or calibration conditional on that selected subset need not transfer to the unverified population.
entries.measured_conclusion: Historical baselines use already-resolved rings, and the current workflow can verify only predictions with later eligible evidence. No frozen verified-versus-unverified representativeness audit quantifies the remaining selection bias.
remaining: Compare prediction-time ring size, era, feature missingness and score distributions across verified, unverified and unscorable cohorts.
Report verified fraction alongside outcomes; do not assign correctness labels to still-unverified cases.

evidence.scope: All eligible already-resolved multi-member rings in legacy heights 0–58,900. Conditional stored labels and whole-snapshot reuse, with fractional tie credit; no forward split.

entries.question: Can we preserve complete retained pool snapshots before rolling deletion, within a fixed storage budget?

task_refs.title: Freeze complete observation cohorts before longer studies.

entries.theoretical_conclusion: Immutable retained snapshots preserve reproducibility and unknown outcomes. They cannot recover earlier missing observations, establish network completeness or validate forecasts. Overlapping archives are not independent samples.
entries.measured_conclusion: A private freeze at 2026-09-12 05:00:09 UTC preserved 651 transactions, 1,437 sightings and 65 polls: 635 confirmed, 11 pending, 5 absent and 0 censored. The 753,664-byte database averaged 11,594.83 allocated bytes per retained poll. Every sighting retained exact fees, weights and local times; node receipt times were unknown. A six-hour timer is deployed on the existing VM with a 2 GiB / 128-archive cap; all three writer PIDs were preserved.
remaining: Reconcile overlapping freezes and follow pending/censored cases under a predeclared forecasting protocol.
Review storage before capacity is reached; the job stops rather than deleting immutable study data.
Durable database commit times and historical effective configuration were not recorded.

evidence.scope: Consistent snapshot of all currently retained pool records, including unknown outcomes. Initial-chain truncation and possible unrecorded earlier pruning remain explicit.

entries.question: Do frozen historical claim values, denominators and source hashes reconcile before publication?
entries.theoretical_conclusion: A claim manifest checks reproducible reporting; it does not validate the scientific assumptions or completeness of the underlying data.
entries.measured_conclusion: 85 declared claims across three frozen historical studies and eight denominator/rate reconciliations pass. Deliberate source-number, source-hash, display-denominator, numeric-prose and unmapped-metric mutations fail. Both static and full release preparation run the offline validator.
remaining: Extend the manifest when adding or changing the frozen historical cards; ledger experiments retain separate evidence checks.
RP2 study/implementation/deployment provenance remains open.
